hints: Translate $|z-3i|\le2$ into the closed disc with centre $(0,3)$ and radius $2$.
Translate the argument bounds into two included rays from $1+2i$, at angles $\pi/4$ and $3\pi/4$ measured from the positive real direction.
Identify the sector between those rays and shade only its intersection with the closed disc.
Draw solid boundaries throughout because all three inequalities include equality.
walkthrough:
Interpret the first inequality $|z - 3\mathrm{i}| \leqslant 2$:
$$\text{Rewrite as } |z - (0 + 3\mathrm{i})| \leqslant 2$$
$$\text{This defines a solid circular disc with centre at } (0, 3) \text{ and radius } R = 2.$$
$$\text{Cartesian boundary equation: } x^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 4$$
$$\text{Key boundary points: } (0, 5), (0, 1), (2, 3), (-2, 3)$$

Interpret the second inequality $\dfrac{\pi}{4} \leqslant \arg(z - 1 - 2\mathrm{i}) \leqslant \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$:
$$\text{Rewrite as } \dfrac{\pi}{4} \leqslant \arg(z - (1 + 2\mathrm{i})) \leqslant \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$$
$$\text{This defines the closed sector between two rays emanating from the vertex point } V(1, 2).$$

Determine the trajectory of the two boundary rays from $V(1, 2)$:
$$\text{Lower ray at angle } \dfrac{\pi}{4} \; (45^{\circ}): \quad y - 2 = 1(x - 1) \implies y = x + 1 \quad (x \geqslant 1)$$
$$\text{At } x = 2: \quad y = 2 + 1 = 3 \implies \text{passes through } (2, 3), \text{ which lies on the circle!}$$
$$\text{Upper ray at angle } \dfrac{3\pi}{4} \; (135^{\circ}): \quad y - 2 = -1(x - 1) \implies y = -x + 3 \quad (x \leqslant 1)$$
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad y = 0 + 3 = 3 \implies \text{passes through } (0, 3), \text{ the circle centre!}$$

Verify the position of the vertex $V(1, 2)$ relative to the circle:
$$\text{Distance from } (0, 3) \text{ to } (1, 2) = \sqrt{(1 - 0)^2 + (2 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 1} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414 < 2$$
$$\text{Hence the vertex } V(1, 2) \text{ lies strictly inside the circle.}$$

Draw the solid circle with centre $(0, 3)$ and radius $2$, plot the solid rays from $(1, 2)$ passing through $(2, 3)$ and $(0, 3)$, and shade the region inside the circle that lies between these two half-lines.
